entry.title: Per-dispatch barrier pair is not coalescible; it brackets a live dispatch
entry.body: Do NOT coalesce the per-dispatch barrier pair in shaderResourceBarrier.cpp on an adjacency argument. ShaderWriteHazardBarrier (:123, allCommands[memoryRead|memoryWrite] -> computeShader[shaderRead|shaderWrite]) runs before each dispatch and ShaderAccessBarrier (:115, computeShader[shaderRead|shaderWrite] -> allCommands[memoryRead|memoryWrite]) runs after it, so the pair brackets a live vkCmdDispatch and the two are not redundant with each other. FACT-0019 shows their apparent adjacency in events.sqlite is an instrumentation artifact. Removing either one on that basis risks silent read-after-write or write-after-read corruption that may only appear in specific scenes, and unlike compiled SRT or dirty-only BDA there is NO shadow-comparison gate available for synchronization changes -- the only check is visual inspection, which cannot prove absence of a race. A narrower change that keeps the dependency but tightens its scope (replacing eAllCommands with the stages that actually produce or consume the dispatch output) is defensible in principle but still needs stage-by-stage justification; CommitBindings calls buffer.Handle() and its full set of recorded side effects was not established. Note these barriers are STRUCTURAL: two per dispatch by design, so at 1361.5 dispatches/epoch they account for 2723 of 4286 barriers/epoch. The way to remove them is to remove dispatches (TASK-0007), not to coalesce them.

entry.title: 88% of dispatches are trivial; top shader runs 40 consecutive, one always exactly 27
entry.body: Compute dispatches are overhead-dominated and highly repetitive, which makes batching the right target. From the per-dispatch GPU timing rows of capture production-20261007-221525 (58 epochs, 92973 compute dispatches, 4214.5 ms total compute GPU time): 82217 dispatches (88.4%) across 86 shaders have a median gpu_ms below 0.02, and together they account for only 471.6 ms, 11.2% of compute GPU time. The three count leaders do almost no GPU work each: 0xe36caa6de7516e57 at 201.9 dispatches/epoch with 0.0056 ms median and 1.127 ms/epoch total; 0x205e6803f8be3e02 at 181.3/epoch, 0.0045 ms median, 0.828 ms/epoch; 0xd138cc3778b66e4d at 111.3/epoch, 0.0041 ms median, 0.580 ms/epoch. Those three are about 494 dispatches per epoch for roughly 2.5 ms of GPU time, while each dispatch also costs CPU recording and two global barriers, so they alone emit around 989 barriers/epoch. REPETITION STRUCTURE, measured as runs of identical consecutive shader in trace order: 0xe36caa6de7516e57 runs 11711 dispatches in only 290 runs, average run 40.4 and max 49; 0x205e6803f8be3e02 is 10516 in 807 runs, average 13.0, max 34; 0xd138cc3778b66e4d is 6453 in 239 runs, average 27.0 with a max of exactly 27, so every single run is 27 long, which strongly suggests a fixed loop over 27 items. Across all compute, 92973 dispatches form 41637 same-shader runs (average 2.23), so collapsing each run to one dispatch would remove 51336, 55.2%. UNPROVEN: consecutive dispatches of one shader are only mergeable if independent, meaning disjoint written ranges; same-shader adjacency alone does not establish that, and WARN-0009 applies to removing the barriers between them.

entry.title: Instrument dispatch dimensions and written ranges to test batchability
entry.body: Instrument consecutive same-shader compute dispatches to test independence, which is the gate on batching (FACT-0020). Log per dispatch: shader hash, thread_group_x/y/z, and the written buffer and storage-image ranges from the prepared bindings, in RenderExecutor::Dispatch at renderCompute.cpp around line 395-415 where has_storage_writes is already computed. Then check whether the written ranges of consecutive dispatches within a run are DISJOINT. If disjoint, two things become available at once: the run can be merged into a single dispatch with proportionally more thread groups plus an index, and the barrier pair between them is provably unnecessary rather than merely suspected, which is what WARN-0009 currently forbids. Start with 0xd138cc3778b66e4d because every one of its runs is exactly 27 long, so a fixed 27-iteration loop is the simplest case to confirm or refute. Note arg4 in the GPU timing CSV is 0 for compute, so dispatch dimensions are not currently recorded anywhere and must be added. Expected payoff if runs are mergeable: up to 55.2% fewer dispatches, each removal saving CPU recording, two global barriers and launch overhead.

entry.title: Three shaders are provably mergeable (14.1% of dispatches); the top one is not
entry.body: Dispatch independence measured per shader: the result is MIXED, and the single biggest dispatcher is NOT mergeable. Instrumentation added for TASK-0010 (KYTY_DISPATCH_RANGES_CSV in renderCompute.cpp logs shader hash, thread-group dimensions and every written buffer range per dispatch) and run on a paused fight, build linked 22:35, analysing the trailing 8 MB of the log = 91230 dispatches, 5961 same-shader runs of length >= 3. DISJOINT, every run, so independently mergeable: 0xd138cc3778b66e4d 265/265 runs disjoint, average run 27.0, groups 10x1x1; 0xb98d678743fe14b8 265/265, average 13.0, groups 1x1x1; 0x88dd24a5711fc450 265/265, average 10.0, groups 245x1x1. OVERLAPPING, no run disjoint, so NOT mergeable as-is: 0xe36caa6de7516e57 0/265 runs disjoint despite the longest average run at 42.4, groups 8x1x1; 0x205e6803f8be3e02 0/658, average 15.3, groups 1x1x1; also 0x2654f1dc72ca08cf, 0x5402c604052b875d and 0xe327a0730ba4f226 all overlapping. The verdicts are not vacuous: the three disjoint shaders log exactly 1.00 written ranges per dispatch and the two overlapping leaders log 2.00, so every dispatch did report writes. This also corrects an optimistic early read -- 0xe36caa6de7516e57 showed distinct base addresses in menu dispatches, but those were non-consecutive; within a fight run its writes overlap. Available saving if the three disjoint shaders' runs each collapse to one dispatch: 7101 -> 265, 3422 -> 265 and 3156 -> 265, removing 12884 of 91230 dispatches, 14.1%, plus two global barriers per removed dispatch (about 25768 barriers). 0xb98d678743fe14b8 is the cleanest case in the set: 13 consecutive dispatches of a SINGLE workgroup each, writing disjoint ranges, which is pure launch overhead. REMAINING GAP: the logger walks program.info.buffers only, so storage-image writes are not captured; if any of the three also writes images the disjointness proof is incomplete and must be extended before merging.

entry.body: EXP-0014's storage-image gap is CLOSED and its three candidates are confirmed safe to merge. RESULT: all three original candidates write ZERO storage images (0.00 images per dispatch), so the buffer-only disjointness in EXP-0014 was already the complete picture for them. TWO MORE FOUND: 0xa3ac56305143f711 336 runs of 4, groups 2x2x16, which does write one storage image per dispatch and whose image bases are disjoint across every run; and 0xfd0d9cc94e4cd5ed 336 runs of 4, groups 1x1x1, no images. CONFIRMED NOT MERGEABLE, overlapping buffer writes and no image writes: 0xe36caa6de7516e57 (335 runs, now averaging 49.0 long), 0x205e6803f8be3e02 (680 runs, 20.7), 0x2654f1dc72ca08cf (336 runs, 8.0), 0x5402c604052b875d (335 runs, 5.0). entry.title: Merge route is hard: dispatch writes are scattered and differently sized
entry.body: Merging the proven-disjoint dispatch runs is NOT a simple grid multiply: the writes are scattered and heterogeneous. Address-pattern analysis of the EXP-0015 slice, first run of each mergeable shader: 0xb98d678743fe14b8 (1x1x1, len 13) writes a uniform 4096 bytes but at scattered bases, deltas including -630784, -16384, -8192, -4096 and +8192, so neither contiguous nor constant-stride. 0xd138cc3778b66e4d (10x1x1, len 27) writes DIFFERENT SIZES per dispatch (9956, 10076, 20888, 61040 bytes) at bases spread over gigabytes. 0x88dd24a5711fc450 (245x1x1, len 10) likewise varies size (1200, 1968, 62664, 183120). 0xa3ac56305143f711 (2x2x16, len 4) is uniform 4096 but jumps by 1048576 and 1114112. Only 0xfd0d9cc94e4cd5ed (1x1x1, len 4) has a constant stride, 256 bytes apart writing 24 bytes each. CONSEQUENCE: these are heterogeneous jobs sharing a shader, not uniform parallel iterations, so a merged dispatch cannot address its output as base + workgroupID * stride. Decisive detail: the two 1x1x1 shaders have a single workgroup per dispatch, so gl_WorkGroupID is always zero and the output location cannot be coming from it at all -- it comes entirely from the per-dispatch descriptor. Merging would require descriptor indexing (an array of buffer descriptors selected by workgroup ID) or a scatter indirection table, which is per-shader work on both the shader and the binding path, for a 14.6% dispatch reduction. This materially lowers the value of the merge route proposed in HYP-0003 and EXP-0015.

entry.title: Elide barriers inside disjoint runs instead of merging; needs read ranges
entry.body: Eliding barriers WITHIN proven-disjoint dispatch runs is a better target than merging them, and it needs one more piece of evidence. FACT-0021 shows merging requires descriptor indexing or a scatter table, per shader, for a 14.6% dispatch cut. But the barrier saving does not depend on merging: if consecutive dispatches in a run provably do not conflict, the ShaderAccessBarrier / ShaderWriteHazardBarrier pair between them is unnecessary, and skipping it needs NO shader or binding change. The saving is the same roughly 35546 barriers EXP-0015 attributed to merging, at a fraction of the work and risk, and it leaves dispatch count and per-dispatch CPU recording untouched. WHAT IS STILL MISSING: EXP-0015 proved disjoint WRITES, which rules out write-after-write hazards only. If dispatch i+1 READS what dispatch i wrote, the barrier is required and removing it corrupts. The logger walks program.info.buffers and program.info.images filtering on .written, so read ranges are not captured. Next step is to log the read ranges too (the same loops without the written filter) and test, per run, whether any dispatch reads a range a previous dispatch in that run wrote. Only if both write-write and read-write are clean does WARN-0009's prohibition lift for these specific shaders, and even then the elision must be keyed on the shader hash being one of the proven set, never applied generally.

entry.title: All five shaders clean on WAW, RAW and WAR across 1138 runs
entry.body: All three hazard classes are clean for the five candidate shaders in a paused fight, so HYP-0005's barrier elision has its evidence. The dispatch logger was extended again on 2026-10-08 to tag every range bw/br/iw/ir, capturing READS as well as writes (buffers lost the .written filter, images lost both the .written and Storage-class filters). A 35 s paused-fight slice gave 441039 rows and 80517 dispatches. For each same-shader run of length >= 3, three tests were run against the accumulated prior ranges within that run: read-after-write (does a dispatch read what an earlier one wrote), write-after-write (disjointness, as in EXP-0015), and write-after-read (does a dispatch write what an earlier one read). RESULT, all three clean on EVERY run: 0xd138cc3778b66e4d 227/227/227 of 227 runs averaging 27.0; 0xb98d678743fe14b8 228/228/228 of 228 runs at 13.0; 0x88dd24a5711fc450 227/227/227 of 227 at 10.0; 0xa3ac56305143f711 228/228/228 of 228 at 4.0; 0xfd0d9cc94e4cd5ed 228/228/228 of 228 at 4.0. 1138 runs total, zero hazards of any class. The WAR test was added only after the first pass omitted it: ShaderWriteHazardBarrier's own comment states it preserves read-before-write ordering, which is precisely write-after-read, so a verdict without that test would have been incomplete on the hazard the barrier exists to prevent. Image ranges remain Base40 plus extent rather than exact byte extents, which over-detects conflict within a single image and therefore errs toward blocking elision, the safe direction. CRITICAL SCOPE LIMIT: this is empirical evidence from ONE paused fight scene, not a static guarantee. Walkouts, menus, replays and other arenas were not sampled, and the same shader could be driven differently there.

entry.title: Dispatch barrier elision fired 17.9%, no FPS gain, reverted
entry.body: Runtime-checked compute barrier elision FIRED on only 17.9% of dispatches and produced no FPS gain, so it was reverted. Implemented 2026-10-08 per HYP-0005: skip the pre-dispatch ShaderWriteHazardBarrier when a CommandBuffer::RecordTicket() comparison proves nothing was recorded since the previous dispatch finished, the buffer is the same, and the current dispatch's read+write ranges do not conflict with the previous dispatch's; the post-dispatch ShaderAccessBarrier was always kept so ordering against later work was unchanged. Measured in a paused fight, capture production-20261008-080640: shaderResourceBarrier.cpp:115 (the always-emitted access barrier, equal to dispatch count) 33543, and :123 (the gated hazard barrier) 27533, so elision fired 6010 times, 17.9%. Previously the two counts were equal. User reported the picture looked correct and no FPS improvement. WHY IT FIRED SO RARELY: between consecutive dispatches, CommitBindings, bindPipeline, ProfilePreparedBufferUses and StartGpuTimer each call buffer.Handle(), bumping the record ticket and breaking the chain. EXP-0016's 1138 hazard-clean runs were clean on WAW/RAW/WAR but those dispatches are NOT adjacent in the recording stream -- the same instrumented-adjacency-versus-reality gap recorded in FACT-0019. NET COST: CollectDispatchRanges ran on every one of the 33543 dispatches, allocating a vector and doing an O(n*m) range comparison, whether or not elision fired, so the change is at best neutral and plausibly a CPU loss. Reverted, keeping only the env-gated LogDispatchRanges diagnostic. The conservative ticket design was correct and is what kept this safe; the lesson is that hazard-freedom does not imply recording-adjacency.

FACT-0021 shows merging requires descriptor indexing or a scatter table, per shader, for a 14.6% dispatch cut. But the barrier saving does not depend on merging: if consecutive dispatches in a run provably do not conflict, the ShaderAccessBarrier / ShaderWriteHazardBarrier pair between them is unnecessary, and skipping it needs NO shader or binding change. The saving is the same roughly 35546 barriers EXP-0015 attributed to merging, at a fraction of the work and risk, and it leaves dispatch count and per-dispatch CPU recording untouched. WHAT IS STILL MISSING: EXP-0015 proved disjoint WRITES, which rules out write-after-write hazards only. If dispatch i+1 READS what dispatch i wrote, the barrier is required and removing it corrupts. The logger walks program.info.buffers and program.info.images filtering on .written, so read ranges are not captured. Next step is to log the read ranges too (the same loops without the written filter) and test, per run, whether any dispatch reads a range a previous dispatch in that run wrote. Only if both write-write and read-write are clean does WARN-0009's prohibition lift for these specific shaders, and even then the elision must be keyed on the shader hash being one of the proven set, never applied generally.

entry.title: Whole-binding reuse across draws is a dead end: 1% hit rate measured
entry.body: Reusing whole prepared bindings across consecutive draws does NOT work for UFC 5: a prior experiment measured a 1% hit rate. Evidence is D:\PS5\bind-reuse.txt, the published scoreboard of the KYTY_BIND_REUSE path: hit 45654, miss_shader 871889, miss_snapshot 1577559, miss_buffer 0, miss_image 0, miss_stream 0, demote 0, hit_percent 1. So the shader hash or binding sizes differ on about 36% of draws, and on the remaining 64% the resource snapshot itself differs. TryReusePreparedBindings in descriptors.cpp requires the shader hash plus all binding sizes to match AND then every snapshot vector to compare equal: buffers, images, samplers, user_data, flattened_srt, specialization_reads and uniform_fill. With 5570 genuinely distinct draws per epoch that test essentially never passes, which is consistent with UFC 5 drawing different objects rather than repeating identical draws. BindReuseEnabled requires KYTY_BIND_REUSE=1 explicitly and additionally refuses to turn on when KYTY_DRAW_COMMIT_THREAD=1, so it is off in every measured configuration and was not contributing to any result recorded today. CONSEQUENCE for TASK-0006: do not pursue caching whole per-draw binding work across draws. The lever has to be making the per-draw work itself cheaper, or caching something with a much narrower and more stable key than the full resource snapshot. This result existed in the working tree but was never in the ledger; recorded 2026-10-08 so it is not re-attempted.

entry.title: Repo has mixed CRLF/LF; preserve per-file endings when scripting edits
entry.body: Line endings in the Kyty tree are MIXED; preserve them per file when patching. Measured 2026-10-08: src/graphics/host_gpu/renderer/colorRenderTarget.cpp is 340 CRLF and 4 bare LF, while src/graphics/host_gpu/renderer/renderCompute.cpp and render.h are LF. A scripted edit that reads with newline='' and writes with newline='\n' silently converts the whole file, producing a diff that touches every line. That is especially damaging here because the working tree carries extensive uncommitted emulator and profiling work, so a whole-file reformat would bury the real change. When patching, read with newline='' , match multi-line patterns using the file's actual terminator (CRLF where applicable), and write back with newline='' so nothing is translated. Verify afterwards by counting CRLF versus bare LF and confirming the ratio is unchanged. Separately, a scripted patch should assert on every pattern before writing anything, so a failed match leaves the file untouched rather than half-edited.

entry.title: Target resolution 96% redundant; derivation is cacheable, image lookup is not
entry.body: Render-target resolution is 96% redundant, but only a third of its cost is skippable without touching image lifetime. Probe added 2026-10-08 (KYTY_RT_RESOLVE_PROBE, counting only, no behaviour change) comparing each ResolveRenderColorTarget call's inputs against the previous call for that slot. Paused fight, 3200001 calls: hit 3074708 (96%), miss_regs 122976 (3.8%), miss_mask 2311 (0.07%), miss_slice 0, first 6. The slice offset NEVER changed between consecutive calls, so the earlier worry that render_target_slice_offset comes from draw args and would churn was unfounded. This is the opposite of FACT-0022's 1% binding-reuse rate, because the key is just the render-target register block plus mask plus slice offset, which changes per render pass rather than per draw (about 262 render passes against 5570 draws). COST SPLIT, from the EXP-0013 fine capture: cpu_resolve_color_target inclusive 1.23 us per call and self 0.40 us per call, at 1.85 calls per draw, so 2.27 us/draw inclusive and 0.74 us/draw self. The self portion is the 298 lines of register validation and layout derivation and is safely cacheable. The remaining 1.5 us/draw is TextureCache::FindImage plus BindRenderTarget, which cannot simply be skipped: FindImage takes m_lock, runs FindImagesInRegion, scans candidates with SameBacking, may run ResolveOverlap, may InsertImage, and may MarkBufferModified, while BindRenderTarget feeds m_bound_images used by the specialization-read overlap checks. FindImage has NO early-out for a repeated identical desc; it redoes the locked range query and candidate scan on every call. AVAILABLE: caching the derivation alone is about 0.74 us/draw = 4.1 ms/epoch = 1.7% of the 246 ms wall. Memoizing FindImage on the same stable key as well would reach about 2.27 us/draw = 12.6 ms/epoch = 5%, and the depth target is a comparable second helping, but that requires reasoning about image lifetime, GC age and layout transitions.

entry.title: Resolve memo cut its target 54% per call; end-to-end gain below scene noise
entry.body: The render-target derivation memo does exactly what it was designed to do, but its end-to-end effect is below scene noise and is NOT established. Implemented 2026-10-08 in colorRenderTarget.cpp: a thread_local 8-slot memo keyed on the render-target register block plus per-slot mask, slice offset, ignore_target_mask and exact_format, storing the pure derivation snapshotted BEFORE the image lookup (FindImage takes desc by reference and may normalise it, so caching the post-call value would not match the uncached path). FindImage and BindRenderTarget still run on every draw, so image lifetime, GC age and m_bound_images are unchanged. KYTY_RT_RESOLVE_CACHE=0 opts out. MEASURED, capture production-20261008-083623 with -FineCpu against the EXP-0013 fine capture: cpu_resolve_color_target self per call fell 0.405 to 0.185 us, a 54% cut, and inclusive per call fell 1.228 to 0.981 us. That is the direct test of the changed code and it passed. HOWEVER the enclosing phase got WORSE: draw_state_cpu median rose 4.20 to 4.70 us, cpu_prepare_draw_state inclusive rose 9.483 to 10.159, and cpu_state_refresh_shaders inclusive rose 5.011 to 6.078 us (+21%) despite being untouched by this change. That last figure is scene variation, which also showed up in the probe hit rate moving from 96% to 88% with miss_regs rising from 122976 to 326127 between the two paused fights. Scene variation therefore exceeds the roughly 1.7% the memo can deliver, so no end-to-end claim is possible; per WARN-0006 the 54% subpath cut must not be reported as an FPS gain. User observed no FPS change, consistent with that.

entry.title: Draw commit worker thread halves FPS: serialized handoff, wait is 1.42x commit
entry.body: KYTY_DRAW_COMMIT_THREAD=1 roughly HALVES the frame rate: it is a serialized handoff, not overlap. Measured 2026-10-08 on the default-on build in a paused fight: present rate fell to 5.16-5.74 fps against about 10.4 fps with the worker off. From its own trace (KYTY_DRAW_COMMIT_TRACE, 772 frames, 408 with more than 100 queued draws): median 188 queued draws per frame, median commit_ms 3.02, median wait_ms 4.29, so wait is 1.42x the commit time. In the fight proper the last frames show 5310 queued draws with commit 52-61 ms and wait 88-113 ms, so the foreground blocks for nearly twice as long as the recording work itself takes. MECHANISM: DrawCommitGate is a single-job handoff, not a parallel recorder. The foreground enqueues one draw's record lambda under a mutex, and CommandBuffer::Handle() calls FinishDrawCommit() whenever the foreground touches the buffer while not on the worker, which the prep phase does for render-target transitions and uploads. So the foreground enqueues and then almost immediately blocks, paying mutex, condition-variable and context-switch cost per draw across 5310 draws per frame while gaining no concurrency. This is the same structural trap as EXP-0017's barrier elision: the recording stream is not partitioned the way the logical phases suggest. The feature is off by default in code so nothing needed reverting; only the environment variable was cleared. Do not enable it, and note it also force-disables BindReuseEnabled, which is irrelevant given FACT-0022.

entry.title: Parallel recording with secondary command buffers; needs concurrent caches
entry.body: Parallel draw recording via SECONDARY command buffers -- the one structural approach today's failures do not rule out. WHY THE EXISTING ATTEMPT FAILED: EXP-0020 showed DrawCommitGate halves FPS because every stage reaches the one shared command buffer through CommandBuffer::Handle(), and Handle() calls FinishDrawCommit(), so the foreground blocks immediately after enqueuing. The serialization point is the SHARED BUFFER, not the work split. DESIGN: allocate one VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_LEVEL_SECONDARY buffer per worker, have each worker record a contiguous RANGE of draws into its own buffer with no shared Handle(), and have the foreground concatenate with vkCmdExecuteCommands at submit. Partition by draw range, never round-robin, because secondary buffers execute in the order they are given and guest draw order must be preserved. CONSTRAINTS ESTABLISHED TODAY: (1) prep is roughly half the per-draw cost, draw_state_cpu 4.7 us plus draw_bindings_cpu 3.0 us against draw_commit_cpu about 6.8 us, so parallelising only the commit caps the win near 45% of recording even with perfect overlap -- the workers must do state and binding derivation too; (2) that derivation reaches the texture cache, buffer cache and pipeline cache, all of which are lock-protected today (TextureCache::FindImage takes m_lock on every call, about 10300 times per epoch), so THE REAL SCOPE IS MAKING THOSE CACHES CONCURRENT, not just splitting the buffer; (3) EmitGlobalBarrier calls EndRendering and runs 1472 times per epoch, and a barrier that tears down the render pass cannot sit inside a secondary buffer recorded against an inherited pass, so global barriers must stay on the foreground and define the partition boundaries; (4) secondary buffers inherit almost no state, and with dynamic rendering each needs VkCommandBufferInheritanceRenderingInfo. BUDGET: recording is 123.58 ms of a 246 ms epoch (FACT-0015). Ideal 4-way parallelism gives about 31 ms, saving roughly 92 ms, a 37% wall cut, which is perhaps 14-16 fps -- still short of the 30 fps floor on its own, so it must be combined with draw-count reduction (TASK-0007). VALIDATE with the reproducible paused-fight baseline and visual inspection; there is no shadow gate for this.

entry.title: Attack the 5570 draws/epoch count, not just per-draw cost
entry.body: Investigate the 5570 draws/epoch draw count itself as a target (EXP-0010). At 38.2 us/draw of instrumented per-draw CPU, halving the draw count is worth about 106 ms/epoch, comparable to any plausible per-draw micro-optimization. Check how many of those draws are redundant, could be batched or instanced, or are state-change-only, and whether UFC 5's render graph repeats passes that could be merged. This is a separate lever from per-draw cost and the two multiply.

entry.title: Cut the 5570 graphics draws per epoch: instrument consecutive draws first
entry.body: Reduce the GRAPHICS draw count from 5570 per epoch, the untested lever with the most headroom. Distinct from the compute dispatch path, which is closed: FACT-0021 (scattered, differently sized writes block merging) and EXP-0017 (barrier elision fires too rarely) apply to compute dispatches only, and nothing equivalent has been measured for graphics draws. WHY IT MATTERS MOST: every draw removed saves its own per-draw CPU (about 22 us of recording at 123.58 ms over 5570 draws), its share of GPU batch time, and its barrier records, so one reduction pays three times, whereas per-draw micro-optimization pays once and has now returned at most 1.7% three attempts running (EXP-0019). FIRST STEP, mirroring what worked for compute: instrument consecutive graphics draws the way KYTY_DISPATCH_RANGES_CSV did, logging per draw the pipeline identity, the render-target key (already proven 88-96% stable by EXP-0018), the vertex and index ranges, and the written attachment ranges, then measure how many consecutive draws differ only in vertex or instance range. Those are the instancing and multi-draw-indirect candidates. Do NOT assume same-pipeline adjacency implies mergeability; FACT-0022 measured whole-binding reuse at a 1% hit rate, so the resources genuinely differ per draw and any batching must index them rather than share them. Also worth checking how many of the 5570 are state-change-only or produce no visible output, since 261.6 render passes per epoch means about 21 draws per pass.

entry.title: Cut draw_state_cpu and draw_bindings_cpu per-draw work
entry.body: Reduce draw_state_cpu and draw_bindings_cpu, which are 77.3% of per-draw CPU at 29.5 us/draw combined (EXP-0010). Per-call medians are small (8.5 and 3.1 us) so the lever is call volume and redundant work per draw, not single-call latency: look for per-draw recomputation that is invariant across a render pass, state that is re-resolved when nothing changed, and binding work that could be cached or diffed against the previous draw. UFC5-only specialization is authorized (DEC-0003). Verify against the now-reproducible paused-fight baseline of 347-350 ms/epoch wall.

entry.title: 30 FPS needs both draw-count reduction and parallel recording
entry.body: Reaching 30 FPS needs BOTH fewer graphics draws and parallel recording; neither is sufficient alone. This REVISES HYP-0003, which named dispatch/draw count reduction as probably the only path. Today closed the compute dispatch half of that: merging is blocked by scattered heterogeneous writes (FACT-0021) and barrier elision fires too rarely to matter (EXP-0017). What remains: (a) the GRAPHICS draw count at 5570 per epoch, untested, which pays three times per draw removed in CPU recording, GPU batch time and barrier records (TASK-0012); and (b) parallel recording via secondary command buffers, whose real scope is making the texture, buffer and pipeline caches concurrent (TASK-0011). Arithmetic for why both: the epoch wall is about 246 ms and 30 fps needs roughly 79 ms at the measured 2.38 presents per epoch, a 3.1x cut. Ideal 4-way parallel recording turns 123.58 ms of recording into about 31 ms, giving roughly 155 ms and perhaps 14-16 fps. Halving the draw count independently cuts recording, GPU and barriers together. Multiplied, the two plausibly reach the floor; separately neither does. Also established today: local per-draw optimization is close to exhausted, three attempts returning at most 1.7% (EXP-0019), and scene variation between paused fights exceeds that, so sub-2% changes are not measurable end to end and should not be pursued for their own sake.

entry.title: Draw/dispatch count reduction is likely the only path to 30 fps
entry.body: Draw/dispatch count reduction is probably the only lever that can reach the 30 fps floor, because it is the only one that cuts CPU recording, GPU work and barrier conservatism simultaneously. Supporting measurements: FACT-0015 shows pure CPU elimination cannot plausibly reach 79 ms/epoch on its own, since zeroing all 172.69 ms of instrumented CPU work still leaves about 84 ms with GPU at 75.88 ms and waits at 40.14 ms. Meanwhile EXP-0010 measured 5570 draws/epoch and the default-on capture shows 1339.6 GPU scope calls per epoch, of which compute is 804.1, render 261.6, copy_copyBuffer 119.7, copy_buffer 69.0, copy_buffer_to_image 40.6 and detile_dispatch 40.6; EXP-0009 also recorded 6045 barrier resource records and 339 command buffers per epoch. Per-draw CPU cost scales with draw count, GPU batch elapsed scales with dispatch count, and barrier records scale with resource transitions per pass, so one reduction pays three times while per-draw micro-optimization pays once. The 804 compute dispatches per epoch are the most striking figure and deserve attention before the render draws. UNTESTED: this assumes a material fraction of those draws and dispatches are redundant, mergeable, instanceable or UFC-5-specific passes that repeat; that has not been examined in code. DEC-0003 authorizes game-specific specialization, which is what makes such merging legitimate here.

entry.title: Lower resolution does not raise FPS; the bottleneck is resolution-independent
entry.body: Lowering output resolution does NOT help frame rate, so fixing the broken 1080p picture would not unlock a win. WARN-0002 says only that the override renders a black scene, which wrongly implies a correctness fix would make it a performance option. The 2026-10-05 experiment in ufc5/resolution-test.md is explicit: with KYTY_VIDEO_OUT_1080P=1 the game selected smaller internal surfaces (1068x600 scene, 1600x900 color/depth, 1920x1080 depth), driver usage fell to about 6456-6560 MiB against a 7249-7296 MiB budget, and the user reported IDENTICAL FPS in the fight. EXP-0002's apparent 10 fps versus 3 fps gap was a residency effect measured while 4K was over budget at 7974 MiB against 7195 MiB and therefore thrashing; bounded LDS has since brought 4K under budget (FACT-0009), so that advantage no longer exists. REASON it cannot help: the bottleneck is host CPU command recording at about 123.58 ms of a roughly 246 ms epoch (FACT-0015), and neither the 5570 draws per epoch nor the per-draw CPU cost changes with render resolution. Resolution reduction cuts GPU work and VRAM residency, and neither is the binding constraint. Keep the override as a diagnostic only, as WARN-0002 says, but do not treat its broken picture as a blocked opportunity.

entry.title: Old branch retired: tooling already ported, sceneDrawDebug deliberately not
entry.body: Cleanup 2026-10-08: the old branch is retired and nothing needed porting from it. The tooling port had ALREADY happened in commit 8c317670 'bring the UFC 5 ledger and tooling onto the upstream-based branch': there are zero .py/.ps1/.sh/.bat files on ufc5-in-game-low-fps that are not in ufc5-v2, and v2's ufc5/ holds 79 files against the old branch's 14. Of the 25 C++ files unique to the old branch, most are upstream restructuring (byteBuffer.h, magicEnum.h, sysVirtual.h, virtualMemory.cpp, gpuResourceManager, rt/hardware, redZonePatcher) since v2 is 99 commits newer; watchedImageTrace, mipTailDiagnostic, imageView_diagnostic, ProbeConfig and dispatchInspector were all built for the NaN and black-round investigation that v2 already resolved (FACT-0005); and gpuTimestamps is superseded by v2's own KYTY_GPU_TIMING stack (FACT-0008). DECIDED NOT TO PORT sceneDrawDebug, reversing an earlier recommendation in this session: it is referenced from five files (renderDraw.cpp, renderCompute.cpp, pipelineCache.cpp, swapchain.cpp, window.cpp) rather than being a self-contained drop-in, it adds NoteDraw and ShouldSuppress calls to the per-draw hot path that is the current bottleneck, its tools/scene_shot.py decoder was never actually committed despite the commit message, and v2 already has a STRONGER capability for the WARN-0007 pixel-proof gap: the detile replay system captures binary output and compares every output byte against a reference with hashes (ufc5/detile-replay.md, capture-detile.ps1, replay-detile.ps1). The branch was pushed to fork/ufc5-in-game-low-fps at 9961a9f1 with all 33 previously unpushed commits, verified byte-identical to the local ref, then deleted locally. Also deleted the stale D:\PS5\ledger.md (256 KB) after verifying all 60 of its section headings appear in the 403 KB src/KytyPS5/ufc5/ledger.md, so it held nothing unique; CLAUDE.md's duplicate-ledger warning section was removed accordingly.

entry.title: Port the GPU test-harness fix: 4 tests blocked on m_gpu==nullptr
entry.body: CORRECTION to FACT-0024: the GPU test-harness commits ARE worth porting, and dropping them was an error. FACT-0005 correctly flagged d68fc246 and 902feded as forward-port candidates; FACT-0024 then concluded 'nothing needed porting' while only reasoning about sceneDrawDebug, and silently dropped the harness commits without justification. EVIDENCE that they matter, measured 2026-10-08: ctest on the committed baseline gives 43% passing, 31 of 54 'failed', but most are Not Run from missing executables. There are 4 genuine failures -- graphics_pipeline_rasterization, pm4_context_state (crash 0xc0000409), compute_meta_clear_classification and texture_cache_image_overlap -- and all 4 abort with 'condition (m_gpu == nullptr) is true' at renderContext.cpp:48. They fail identically with every one of today's opt-outs set (KYTY_COMPILED_SRT=0, KYTY_BDA_SYNC=0, KYTY_BARRIER_COALESCE=0, KYTY_RT_RESOLVE_CACHE=0), so they are NOT caused by today's work. Separately, stream_buffer_ring and buffer_cache_ranges failed only under ctest -j 4 and pass serially with today's changes enabled, so those two are parallel-execution flakes, not regressions. d68fc246 is precisely the fix: it adds RenderContext::HasGpu() and RenderContext::DiagnosticFrameNum(), the latter returning 0 rather than aborting when no GuestGpu is attached, with a comment stating that unconditional GetGpu().GetFrameNum() calls on the dispatch path made every GPU test abort before running. v2 has 19 such call sites and neither helper. PORT SIZE roughly 50 lines across 7 files (renderContext.h/.cpp, bufferCache.cpp, descriptors.cpp, renderCompute.cpp, renderDraw.cpp, swapchain.cpp) plus 8 lines in ShaderRecompilerComputeTests.cpp from 902feded. WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the 4 blocked tests cover the texture cache, pipeline rasterization, pm4 context state and compute meta clear -- exactly the areas TASK-0011 and TASK-0012 would disturb -- so porting this converts unusable tests into the regression net that structural work lacks. The old branch is deleted locally but the objects remain reachable and the branch is preserved at fork/ufc5-in-game-low-fps 9961a9f1.

entry.title: Tests were never built (EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL); fresh build gives 4 of 6, 1 real PM4 bug
entry.body: The test suite was never being built, so every earlier test number in this session was measured on stale binaries. All test targets are EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL in CMakeLists.txt (line 367 and the add_executable calls that follow), so 'cmake --build _Build/windows' silently builds none of them. The 12 test executables present were dated 08:05 through 23:59 across previous days while today's edits landed at 09:27, which invalidates three claims made earlier: the '43% passed, 31 of 54 failed' figure, the conclusion that the four failures persisted 'identically with every opt-out set' (those binaries could not read the new flags at all), and the diagnosis of stream_buffer_ring and buffer_cache_ranges as parallel-execution flakes. Only one earlier conclusion survives, and for a stronger reason than given: the failures cannot have been caused by today's work because the binaries predate it entirely. AFTER building explicitly with 'cmake --build _Build/windows --target shader_recompiler_compute_tests -j 8' (57 steps, links the whole emulator per test binary, which is why they are excluded from the default build), 4 of 6 relevant tests PASS: graphics_pipeline_rasterization, compute_meta_clear_classification, texture_cache_image_overlap and graphics_draw_offsets. The m_gpu == nullptr abort at renderContext.cpp:48 is gone. Two still fail, both reported as exit 0xc0000409, which is __fastfail from a test assertion rather than stack corruption: pm4_context_state and shader_recompiler_compute (the unfiltered run, which includes it). The real message is 'Pm4NativeTargetGeometry failed at legacy register holes: a removed GCN register has a handler or a native packet is not handled'. That Require checks three conditions -- legacy GCN shader slots 0x0cb-0x0eb plus a named list having null handlers, SPI_SHADER_PACE_ID_PS/GS and COMPUTE_PACE_ID having indirect handlers, and a VGT_INDEX_TYPE SET_UCONFIG_REG_INDEX packet processing to Complete with VGT_INDEX_TYPE and IA_MULTI_VGT_PARAM handled. Which one fails was not determined: all five registers are referenced in pm4Handlers.cpp and the legacy hole has no direct index registrations, so the registration is likely table-driven and needs instrumentation to isolate. This is a PRE-EXISTING issue in the uncommitted pm4Handlers work, not from today.

entry.title: Diagnose the pre-existing Pm4NativeTargetGeometry register-hole failure
entry.body: Diagnose the Pm4NativeTargetGeometry 'legacy register holes' assertion, which is the only real test failure and predates today's work (EXP-0021). Reproduce with: cmake --build _Build/windows --target shader_recompiler_compute_tests -j 8, then ctest -R pm4_context_state --output-on-failure. The Require checks three conditions and any one of them failing produces the same message, so the first step is to split it or print each sub-result: (a) legacy GCN shader slots, the named legacy_shader_slots list plus the 0x0cb-0x0eb range, must have null entries in BOTH g_hw_sh_func and g_hw_sh_indirect_func; (b) SPI_SHADER_PACE_ID_PS, SPI_SHADER_PACE_ID_GS and COMPUTE_PACE_ID must have non-null g_hw_sh_indirect_func entries; (c) a SET_UCONFIG_REG_INDEX packet carrying VGT_INDEX_TYPE must Process to Complete with VGT_INDEX_TYPE and IA_MULTI_VGT_PARAM handled in both the direct and indirect tables. Grep is not sufficient to tell which: all five registers are referenced in pm4Handlers.cpp and the 0x0cb-0x0eb range has no direct index registrations, so the tables are likely filled programmatically. The failure matters because pm4Handlers.cpp carries substantial uncommitted work and a wrongly registered or missing PM4 register handler can silently mis-handle guest state, which is the class of bug least likely to be caught by looking at the screen.

entry.title: Frame budget closes to 96%; translation (19%) and waits (19%) unattributed
entry.body: Full frame budget with closure, and TWO chunks of about 19% each remain unattributed. From capture production-20261008-083623 (30 epochs, -FineCpu so profiler cost is inflated), wall 283.5 ms/epoch of which the profiler itself is 33.96 ms (flush 24.62 plus collect 9.34), giving a real wall near 250 ms. entry.title: The dark 19% of wall is probably uninstrumented garbage collection
entry.body: The unattributed ~19% of epoch wall (translation_other_cpu, 46.88 ms) is probably garbage collection. Reasoning: FACT-0026 defines translation_other_cpu as guest CPU inside the process slice but outside the recording scopes. guest_process_slice is a single scope at graphicsRun.cpp:768 wrapping GuestGpu::Process, and Process calls m_renderer.RunGarbageCollector() on every completed submission. RenderContext::RunGarbageCollector runs four phases -- BufferCache::ProcessFaultBuffer, TextureCache::ProcessDownloadImages, TextureCache::RunGarbageCollector and BufferCache::RunGarbageCollector -- and NONE of them carries a ProfileCpuScope or ProfileDetailScope, verified by grepping their entries. They are therefore completely invisible to the profiler while sitting exactly where the dark time is. The fine-CPU data cannot see them either: its outside_draw phase totals only 8.49 ms against the state, bindings and commit phases at 362, 344 and 275 ms. SUPPORTING PRIOR EVIDENCE: the legacy ledger records KYTY_TEXGC_BUDGET_FIX taking texture GC from 3 ms to 71 ms with the GC running about 175 times per frame, and that flag is listed among the measured regressions cleared explicitly by the launcher, so GC cost has been pathological in this title before. Instrumentation added 2026-10-08: ProfileCpuScope gc_total wrapping the function plus gc_fault_buffer, gc_download_images, gc_texture_cache and gc_buffer_cache per phase. UNTESTED -- if GC turns out to be small, the remaining candidates inside Process are the PM4 packet dispatch itself (register writes through the jump tables) and cp.BufferInit/BufferFlush.

entry.title: All foreground wait is one line: bufferCache.cpp:276, a 50.77 ms/epoch queue drain
entry.body: The entire foreground wait is ONE call site, and it is a GPU queue drain. Re-attributed for free from capture production-20261008-102116's wait-sites.csv, no new run needed. bufferCache.cpp:276 on the foreground thread (31588): 953 calls, 6092.7 ms union, 50.77 ms/epoch, max single call 55.0 ms, about 8 calls per epoch averaging 6.4 ms. The per-frame foreground_explicit_wait median is 50.93 ms/epoch, so this single site IS essentially the whole 18.2%. The other large wait, commandScheduler.cpp:387 at 109.43 ms/epoch over 18655 calls, is on background thread 29148 -- the scheduler waiting on the GPU, which is expected and does not block the guest. MECHANISM: line 276 is m_scheduler.Wait(tick) in the SYNCHRONOUS branch of BufferCache::DownloadBufferMemory, reached from ReadMemory via DownloadBufferMemory<false> at line 379. The tick is m_scheduler.CurrentTick(), so the readback copy sits at the back of the GPU queue and the foreground thread waits for EVERYTHING ahead of it to complete. It is a queue drain, not a dependency stall. It must be synchronous for correctness: ReadMemory runs when the guest CPU faults reading GPU-written memory, so the guest cannot proceed without the data. An ASYNC path already exists in the same function (DownloadBufferMemory<true>, which calls DeferPriorityOperation instead of waiting) but is only used at line 798, so v2 is less short of deferred-readback machinery than FACT-0008 implied. THIS IS THE MOST CONCENTRATED COST IN THE FRAME: 50.77 ms/epoch, roughly 20% of the real ~250 ms wall, in one line. Candidate remedies: a dedicated transfer queue so the copy does not queue behind graphics work (the old branch's 847e20f9, preserved at fork/ufc5-in-game-low-fps; note the launcher records KYTY_XFER_QUEUE as measured neutral, but that was pre-LDS), or TASK-0002's earlier-writer approach, waiting on the writer's tick rather than the current one.

entry.title: 38% of foreground wait is a recoverable queue drain; 62% is unsubmitted work
entry.body: Writer-bounds tracing splits the foreground wait cleanly: 38% is a recoverable queue drain, 62% is a genuine unsubmitted-work stall. Capture production-20261008-125601 with -Lifetime (32 epochs analysed; wall 372.5 ms/epoch and foreground wait 81.64 ms/epoch because lifetime tracing is heavy, so use this for DEPENDENCY structure, not rates). 957 transactions, ZERO event drops, so coverage is complete. Three guest addresses own the entire foreground wait, matching EXP-0005's pre-LDS writer trace: 0x1164b80000 with 240 calls, 239 ELIGIBLE and 239 earlier_than_tail, 1113.0 ms wait of which 1091.4 ms (98.1%) is bounded by a writer that completed earlier than the queue tail; 0x1165e00000 with 239 calls, 238 eligible, 239.0 ms wait and 238.3 ms (99.7%) recoverable; and 0x1140008000 with 478 calls, ZERO eligible, 2152.9 ms wait and NOTHING recoverable. Ineligibility reasons tally exactly to that address: overlapping_bound_write_pending 478 and required_tick_unsubmitted 478, plus missing_writer_coverage 2 and submit_not_returned_at_checkpoint 126. CONCLUSION: 1329.7 of 3505.0 ms, 37.9% of foreground wait, is the foreground draining a GPU queue for data whose writer had already finished -- recoverable in principle by waiting on the writer's tick instead of CurrentTick, or by a dedicated transfer queue. Projected onto the lighter baseline's 50.93 ms/epoch that is about 19.3 ms/epoch, roughly 7.7% of a 250 ms wall. The other 62% is 0x1140008000, the indirect-args address EXP-0005 described as needing current unsubmitted recording work: the guest reads arguments before the producing work exists, so no queue scheduling can recover it. CAVEAT from the analyzer itself: eligibility is an observed conservative dependency bound, not proof of safe transfer-queue execution or recoverable wait; declared writers overapproximate stores, and queue-family sharing, aliases and CPU publication still need validation (WARN-0005).

entry.title: shadPS4 readbacks: 30x more calls at 94x lower cost; their batching fix does not transfer
entry.body: Cross-project comparison with shadPS4: our readback problem is the OPPOSITE shape to theirs, so their proposed fix would not help us. From shadPS4 upstream RFC issue 4316 (Bloodborne gameplay, RTX 5090 / Ryzen 7950X3D, Precise readback mode): about 106 BufferCache::ReadMemory calls per frame, about 68 us per call, 7.23 ms of CPU stall per frame; a DriveClub race measured 19.1 Finish per frame and 2.76 ms/f. Kyty on UFC 5 (RTX 3070): about 8 readback calls per epoch at roughly 6400 us each for 50.77 ms/epoch, which at the measured 2.38 presents per epoch is about 3.4 calls and 21 ms per frame. So we make roughly 30x FEWER readback calls but each costs about 94x MORE, and our total stall is about 3x worse. Hardware difference (5090 versus 3070) cannot explain 94x. INTERPRETATION: shadPS4 calls Scheduler::Finish very frequently, which keeps the GPU queue shallow so each drain is cheap; Kyty calls it rarely against a queue holding roughly 77.91 ms/epoch of GPU work, so each drain is expensive. Their RFC proposes a Batched mode coalescing ReadMemory calls within a fault window into one Finish -- that is a fix for call COUNT, which we do not have; ours is a fix for per-call COST, which points back at EXP-0023's finding that 38% of our wait is a recoverable queue drain. The RFC mentions neither a dedicated transfer queue nor waiting on an earlier writer's tick, so those remain unexplored in that project too. USEFUL CONTEXT: shadPS4 ships readbacks experimental and OFF by default since v0.10.0, and Precise mode is hidden in advanced settings because it costs performance and hangs some titles including Bloodborne, with about 12 FPS loss reported on AMD. Guest-CPU-reads-GPU-memory is therefore a known-hard unsolved problem across PS4/PS5 emulation, not an obvious trick we are missing.

entry.title: DXVK: hand off chunks not draws; our 17.5 draws/submit is 3-6x too fine
entry.body: DXVK's command-stream design explains exactly why EXP-0020's draw-commit worker halved our frame rate: we split at the wrong seam. DXVK (a D3D-to-Vulkan translation layer, so it shares our constraint of being unable to change the application's draw pattern) does deferred recording successfully. Per its developer guidelines, the application thread fills 16 KiB DxvkCsChunk buffers with PRE-PROCESSED COMMANDS -- it never touches a Vulkan command buffer -- and 'submitting a command list is cheap because our implementation will just forward those chunks to a background worker'. The CS thread then owns the Vulkan recording exclusively. Kyty's DrawCommitGate did the opposite: both the foreground and the worker reach the same command buffer through CommandBuffer::Handle(), and Handle() calls FinishDrawCommit(), so the foreground blocked immediately after enqueuing and paid mutex plus context-switch cost per draw across 5310 draws per frame (EXP-0020, wait 1.42x commit). THE LESSON for TASK-0011: do not hand off per-draw work. Hand off a chunk, and ensure the producer NEVER needs the recorded buffer back. That means PM4 handlers would translate guest packets into an intermediate chunk format rather than calling renderer methods that record directly, which is a larger inversion than secondary command buffers alone but is the design that is proven at scale. SUBMISSION GRANULARITY, a second quantified finding: DXVK's guidelines recommend recording at least 50-100 draws into each command list. Kyty does 5570 draws across 317.7 submits per epoch, which is 17.5 draws per submit -- roughly 3x to 6x finer than that guidance. That ties directly to EXP-0024's cp_buffer_flush at 18.67 ms/epoch and would also shrink the queue depth that makes the readback drain expensive (FACT-0027, FACT-0028). CONFIRMS the readback conclusion too: DXVK still forces the app thread to wait for the worker on Map and readback calls, 'which is why the design minimizes them', and DXVK 2.0 only 'reduced unnecessary worker thread synchronization around resource readbacks' rather than removing the wait.

entry.title: 100% of submissions are our policy, zero guest-required; 16.9 draws/submit vs DXVK's 50-100
entry.body: EVERY command-buffer submission in a paused fight is our own policy, not a guest requirement -- so submission batching is a tuning knob, not a correctness gamble. BufferFlush was given a reason label and the three guest end-of-pipe sites in pm4Handlers.cpp were tagged cp_flush_eop. Capture production-20261008-141300 (54 epochs): cp_buffer_flush 329.6 calls/epoch, 20.26 ms/epoch, 61.5 us per call; cp_flush_eop ZERO calls. So 100% of submissions and 100% of submission time come from graphicsRun.cpp:865, which flushes after any guest submission that made progress, and none come from the release_mem interrupt path where the guest actually asks to observe completion. WHY THIS MATTERS: at 5570 draws across 329.6 submits we record 16.9 draws per submit, while DXVK's own guidance (FACT-0029) is 50-100 draws per command list, so we submit 3x to 6x more often than a mature translation layer recommends. Because no EOP interrupt is requested, the guest is not observing GPU completion at these boundaries, so deferring the Vulkan submit across several guest submissions should preserve observable behaviour provided we still submit before anything that waits: an EOP or fence, a readback (bufferCache.cpp:276 calls Wait), or present. PROJECTED: batching to 50-100 draws per submit would cut 329.6 submits to roughly 60-110, reclaiming perhaps 13-16 ms of the 20.26 ms, AND shrinking the queue depth that makes each readback drain cost 6.4 ms, which EXP-0023 measured as 38% recoverable of 50.9 ms. Combined plausible reach is 25-30 ms/epoch, around 10-12% of wall, from a policy change rather than an architecture rewrite. SCOPE LIMIT: zero EOP flushes were observed in THIS paused fight only. Menus, loading, walkouts and replays were not sampled and may request them, so the lazy-flush trigger must still honour EOP rather than assume it never happens.

entry.title: Lazy submission: submits 340->46, waits fell 13 ms, FPS gain unconfirmed
entry.body: Lazy submission works mechanically and improves the wall metric, but the FPS gain is NOT yet confirmed. Implemented in CommandProcessor::BufferFlush: accumulate across guest submissions and submit at 64 draws, with guest EOP always submitting and KYTY_SUBMIT_DRAW_THRESHOLD=0 restoring the old behaviour. Safety rested on CommandScheduler::Wait calling Submit() when the requested tick is current and Finish() submitting before waiting, so the readback path at bufferCache.cpp:276 self-flushes and cannot deadlock. MECHANISM CONFIRMED, capture production-20261008-141838 (99 epochs) against production-20261008-133226 (117 epochs): queue_submits 340 -> 46 per epoch (-86%); the cp_buffer_flush scope still runs 325.6 times per epoch but most calls now return early, so its cost fell from 61.5 to 13.4 us per call and 20.26 to 4.37 ms per epoch; submit_cpu 8.94 -> 2.52; translation_other 45.78 -> 38.47. My prediction that cost would shift into waits was WRONG in the right direction: foreground waits FELL 52.73 -> 39.61 ms, so fewer and larger submissions reduced waiting rather than deepening the queue. recording was unchanged at 120.94 versus 120.63 and GPU union barely moved, 77.91 -> 74.90. CAUTION ON THE HEADLINE: wall fell 273.40 -> 244.06, a 29.34 ms drop, but profiler overhead also fell 41.15 -> 32.61 ms because fewer submissions emit fewer events, so about 8.5 ms of that is instrumentation artifact and the real improvement is nearer 20.8 ms/epoch. Implied present rate rises 7.32 -> 8.19 /s profiled, or 8.61 -> 9.46 /s unprofiled, about +10%. HOWEVER the user observed no FPS improvement (9.88 and 10.47 against a roughly 10.0-10.4 baseline), and the picture looked correct. Scene variation between captures has repeatedly been this large today, so this needs a same-build back-to-back A/B of KYTY_SUBMIT_DRAW_THRESHOLD=0 against the default before any gain is claimed, per WARN-0006. The change is left enabled pending that.

entry.title: A-B-A confirms lazy submission: +10-19% in fight, roughly +46% in menus
entry.body: CONFIRMED by A-B-A: lazy submission is a real causal gain, and it is much larger outside the paused fight. Same build, unprofiled, FPS sampled over 45 s per leg from the PresentRate log, alternating KYTY_SUBMIT_DRAW_THRESHOLD=0 (control, submit per guest submission) against the default 64. PAUSED FIGHT medians: A control 8.59, B test 10.22, A-prime control 9.29. The two control legs differ by 0.70 fps (7.8%), which is the scene-variance floor for single-run comparisons and retroactively justifies refusing to claim the 1.7% resolve-memo result. Test exceeds BOTH control legs, so the effect is causal: +14.3% against the control mean, +10.0% against the better control leg as a conservative bound, +19.0% against the worse. MENUS, user observation on the way to each fight: control 40-41, test 54-60, return-control 30-41. Test exceeds both control legs there too, roughly +40 to +50%, and the 60 may be a refresh cap rather than the ceiling. WHY THE MENU GAIN IS LARGER: submission cost is per-submission and independent of how much work each carries. In the fight, 5570 draws per epoch mean recording dominates and submission was only about 20 ms of 273; in menus there are few draws per submission so submission overhead is proportionally far greater. METHOD LESSON: the whole session optimised and measured against the paused fight alone, and that hid a roughly 46% menu improvement entirely. The user noticed it from the title screen before reaching the fight. Future performance work should sample menus and walkouts as well, not only the paused fight (compare FACT-0014, where live gameplay also turned out faster than paused).

entry.title: Descriptor buffers are the best-evidenced lever; our draw count looks normal for a heavy scene
entry.body: Research 2026-10-08: descriptor handling is the best-evidenced remaining lever for the recording block, and our draw count appears high but not clearly pathological. DESCRIPTOR WORK: vkd3d-proton's release notes call VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer 'significant in that it removes a ton of CPU overhead', its 2.6 notes say descriptor copies are 'a key contributor to CPU overhead in D3D12', and a third-party write-up states vkd3d-proton 'went to hell and back to optimize this case because in many titles it was the number 1 performance overhead'. It also uses bindless shader-visible heaps (VKD3D_MIN_VIEW_DESCRIPTOR_COUNT of 1000000, UpdateAfterBind) and recommends VK_VALVE_mutable_descriptor_type for CPU overhead. RELEVANCE: Kyty writes descriptor sets per draw in RenderExecutor::CommitBindings, building m_descriptor_writes/_buffers/_images each time, which is exactly the pattern descriptor buffers remove. Per-draw phases measured in EXP-0010 and later: draw_commit_cpu 6.8 us is the LARGEST, draw_bindings_cpu 3.0, draw_state_cpu 4.7, so bindings plus commit are about 9.8 us/draw or roughly 55 ms/epoch at 5570 draws. Descriptor buffers could cut both, since binding by offset removes per-draw vkCmdBindDescriptorSets as well as the set writes. CAVEAT from the same sources: there is no array form of GetDescriptorEXT, so 'in the extreme cases, descriptor buffers can actually have worse CPU overhead than legacy model'. DRAW COUNT: no published per-frame host draw count was found for RPCS3 or shadPS4. Indirect evidence only -- RPCS3 gates FIFO preprocessing on saving at least 500 draw calls above 2000, and raised its draw-call resource pool from 4K to 16K for heavy scenes, so a few thousand draws per frame is normal there; shadPS4 maps PS4 draw packets directly to rasterizer draws and recently added draw and dispatch counters to its frame overlay, which is the way to get a real comparison. Kyty's 5570 draws/epoch is about 2800 per frame at 2.0 presents/epoch, which is within RPCS3's heavy-scene range, so the count is probably the game's rather than ours. That weakens TASK-0012's premise and strengthens making each draw cheaper instead.

entry.title: 98.7% of draws already push descriptors; descriptor-buffer migration withdrawn
entry.body: Descriptor buffers are NOT worth migrating to: 98.7% of draws already take the push-descriptor fast path. Probe added to RenderExecutor::CommitBindings (KYTY_DESCRIPTOR_PATH_PROBE, counting only) and run in a paused fight: push 2269413, heap 30588, total 2300001, so the heap path is 1.3% of draws. mean_writes_push 3.18, mean_writes_heap 12.90, max_writes 14. WHY THIS CLOSES IT: pushDescriptorSetKHR skips descriptor set allocation and vkUpdateDescriptorSets entirely, so the cost VKD3D-Proton eliminated with VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer -- which its notes call removing 'a ton of CPU overhead' and which a third-party write-up called 'the number 1 performance overhead' in many titles -- is a cost we are almost never paying. Their problem came from D3D12's descriptor-heap and CopyDescriptorsSimple model; Kyty has no equivalent. Eliminating the remaining 1.3% entirely would be worth about 1.3% of descriptor cost, which is noise. NOTE a curiosity worth remembering: max_writes is 14 across 2.3 million draws, well under the 3070's maxPushDescriptors of 32, yet 30588 draws still fell to the heap. That is because shaders.cpp:199 decides uses_push_descriptors per PIPELINE from the summed descriptorCount of the layout bindings including array sizes, not from the writes a draw actually performs. A layout declaring more than 32 descriptors cannot be a push-descriptor layout even when only 14 are ever written. Not worth pursuing at 1.3%, but it explains the split. CONSEQUENCE: the 9.8 us/draw in draw_bindings_cpu plus draw_commit_cpu is NOT descriptor set management. It is the per-draw resource resolution (PrepareBindings, FindBuffers, RebindImages/Buffers, resolve_texture, buffer_synchronize) plus the driver calls themselves (pushDescriptorSetKHR, bindPipeline, bindVertexBuffers, the draw). That is diffuse work, consistent with three failed attempts to reduce it locally, and it means recording cost is reducible only by doing the same work on more threads -- the DXVK chunk-handoff model in TASK-0011 -- not by a cheaper binding model. FACT-0030's descriptor recommendation is therefore withdrawn.

entry.title: Descriptor buffers are the best-evidenced lever; our draw count looks normal for a heavy scene
entry.body: Research 2026-10-08: descriptor handling is the best-evidenced remaining lever for the recording block, and our draw count appears high but not clearly pathological. DESCRIPTOR WORK: vkd3d-proton's release notes call VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer 'significant in that it removes a ton of CPU overhead', its 2.6 notes say descriptor copies are 'a key contributor to CPU overhead in D3D12', and a third-party write-up states vkd3d-proton 'went to hell and back to optimize this case because in many titles it was the number 1 performance overhead'. It also uses bindless shader-visible heaps (VKD3D_MIN_VIEW_DESCRIPTOR_COUNT of 1000000, UpdateAfterBind) and recommends VK_VALVE_mutable_descriptor_type for CPU overhead. RELEVANCE: Kyty writes descriptor sets per draw in RenderExecutor::CommitBindings, building m_descriptor_writes/_buffers/_images each time, which is exactly the pattern descriptor buffers remove. Per-draw phases measured in EXP-0010 and later: draw_commit_cpu 6.8 us is the LARGEST, draw_bindings_cpu 3.0, draw_state_cpu 4.7, so bindings plus commit are about 9.8 us/draw or roughly 55 ms/epoch at 5570 draws. Descriptor buffers could cut both, since binding by offset removes per-draw vkCmdBindDescriptorSets as well as the set writes. CAVEAT from the same sources: there is no array form of GetDescriptorEXT, so 'in the extreme cases, descriptor buffers can actually have worse CPU overhead than legacy model'. DRAW COUNT: no published per-frame host draw count was found for RPCS3 or shadPS4. Indirect evidence only -- RPCS3 gates FIFO preprocessing on saving at least 500 draw calls above 2000, and raised its draw-call resource pool from 4K to 16K for heavy scenes, so a few thousand draws per frame is normal there; shadPS4 maps PS4 draw packets directly to rasterizer draws and recently added draw and dispatch counters to its frame overlay, which is the way to get a real comparison. Kyty's 5570 draws/epoch is about 2800 per frame at 2.0 presents/epoch, which is within RPCS3's heavy-scene range, so the count is probably the game's rather than ours. That weakens TASK-0012's premise and strengthens making each draw cheaper instead.

entry.title: Stage 1 scoped: 3 blocking Handle() sites of 35, not 94
entry.body: TASK-0011 Stage 1 is tractable: only THREE call sites genuinely block 'the producer never records'. A defaulted std::source_location on CommandBuffer::Handle() attributes every caller. Measured in a paused fight: 14400001 Handle() calls across 35 exercised sites, not the 94 that exist in source. Six sites are 85% of all calls. CLASSIFIED: renderDraw.cpp:689 at 3168696 (22%) is the colour render-target transition inside resolution and MUST move to a chunk stream; renderDraw.cpp:752 at 1987755 (14%) is the depth transition, same; graphicsRun.cpp:1637 at 1298419 (9%) is EmitGlobalBarrier's ProfilePipelineBarrier2, which must move or stay as an explicit sync point since it already calls EndRendering. The other three do NOT block: descriptors.cpp:1407 at 2618508 (18%) is CommitBindings taking the buffer to record binds, which is the worker's job by design; renderDraw.cpp:1360 at 2101850 (15%) captures the handle into the commit work packet and would simply stop capturing one; and sync.cpp:80 at 1073783 (7%) is '(void)buffer.Handle();' which discards the result and exists only for Handle()'s side effects, recording nothing. The resource caches barely feature: bufferCache 2.9%, streamBuffer 0.8%, image.cpp 0.1%, so the remaining 15% tail can force a sync point when it fires rather than needing a chunk representation. CONSEQUENCE: Stage 1 is roughly three conversions plus a chunk format, not the 94-site multi-week inversion feared. STAGING, with per-draw arithmetic from EXP-0010: resolution (state 4.7 + bindings 3.0 + targets 1.1 + vertex_index 0.4 + pipeline 0.4 = 9.6 us/draw = 53.5 ms/epoch) and commit (6.8 us/draw = 37.9 ms/epoch). Stage 1 is chunk record-then-replay still single-threaded, which should be behaviour-identical and near performance-neutral and PROVES THE SEAM that EXP-0020 skipped. Stage 2 is one commit worker overlapping the two, worth about 38 ms or +16%. Stage 3 is concurrent caches and N workers for the rest.

entry.title: Stage 1 increment: 91% fewer producer buffer touches; FPS neutrality unconfirmed
entry.body: TASK-0011 Stage 1, first increment: the producer now skips the command buffer on ~91% of render-target transitions. Image::Transit gained an overload taking CommandBuffer& instead of vk::CommandBuffer, so Handle() is called only after GetBarriers proves work is needed; the old signature evaluated Handle() as an ARGUMENT, before the empty check. The two hot sites in renderDraw.cpp (colour and depth target transitions) now use it. VERIFIED by the Handle()-caller probe: renderDraw.cpp:689 and :752 were 3168696 and 1987755 calls, 35.8% of all 14.4M Handle() calls, and are now ABSENT entirely, replaced by image.cpp:332 at 619189, which is 3.1% of that run's 20.2M. Normalised for run length that is a 91% reduction in share, confirming roughly nine in ten of those calls recorded nothing. Picture confirmed correct by the user, no corruption. UNINTENDED SIDE EFFECT, important: barrier_global fell from 4286.2 to 2437.5 per epoch, -43%. The mechanism is that barrier coalescing (EXP-0013) skips when nothing was recorded since the last barrier, keyed on the dirty flag Handle() sets, and Transit's argument evaluation was previously setting that flag even when Transit recorded nothing. Those were FALSE dirty marks making coalescing over-conservative, so the extra skipping is legitimate by the original argument that Handle() remains the only route to the buffer. barrier_image 751.7 -> 683.4 and barrier_buffer 914.9 -> 668.8 also fell, though those references come from a capture with a different feature set. NOT ESTABLISHED: FPS read 9.18-9.45 against a roughly 10.2 baseline, about 10% down, which sits at the edge of the 7.8% single-run variance floor measured in EXP-0027. The sample was only 3-4 windows and a longer sample could not be taken. The change removes work rather than adding it, so a real regression has no obvious mechanism, but neutrality is NOT confirmed and should be A-B tested before Stage 2 results are attributed.

entry.title: Stage 1 completion: ordered operation queue with a chunk arena
entry.body: TASK-0011 Stage 1 completion: replace DrawCommitGate's single job slot with an ordered operation queue. WHY THIS IS THE REMAINING BLOCKER: the third blocking Handle() site is graphicsRun.cpp:1637, EmitGlobalBarrier's ProfilePipelineBarrier2, and unlike the transitions fixed in EXP-0029 it genuinely records, so it cannot simply be deferred. Leaving it as an inline sync point would stall the worker about every 2.3 draws (2437.5 barriers against 5570 draws per epoch), which is precisely the failure EXP-0020 measured as wait being 1.42x commit. DESIGN. (1) Ordered queue of operations, not one job: today DrawCommitGate holds a single std::function m_job and Wait() blocks on it. It needs a FIFO the producer appends to and the worker drains in order, with the operation kinds being draw, global barrier, image transition and end-rendering, so relative order is preserved without the producer recording anything. (2) Chunk arena, not per-item allocation: renderDraw.cpp currently does std::make_shared<CommitWork>() per draw, a heap allocation on each of 5570 draws per epoch. DXVK buffers pre-processed commands in 16 KiB chunks for this reason (FACT-0029); copy that rather than queueing shared_ptrs. (3) The producer must stop acquiring the handle: work->vk = buffer.Handle() at renderDraw.cpp:1360 captures it today (15% of all Handle() calls) and the worker should acquire it itself. (4) Flush points: submit, any Wait (CommandScheduler::Wait already calls Submit when the tick is current), present, and a queue-full backpressure limit. STAGING, because a half-finished state does not run: first land the queue SINGLE-THREADED, with the producer appending and the drain happening immediately at the same points, which should be behaviour-identical and near performance-neutral and proves the seam EXP-0020 skipped. Only then move the drain to a worker, which is where the roughly 38 ms or +16% from overlapping resolution (53.5 ms) with commit (37.9 ms) appears. PREREQUISITE before attributing any Stage 2 result: A-B the EXP-0029 commit, whose FPS neutrality is unconfirmed (9.18-9.45 against a roughly 10.2 baseline, inside the 7.8% variance floor).
